paragraphs.text: And Jesus went out from the temple, and was going on his way; and his disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἐπορεύετο, καὶ προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπιδεῖξαι αὐτῷ τὰς οἰκοδομὰς τοῦ ἱεροῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Kai exelthōn ho Iēsous apo tou hierou eporeueto, kai prosēlthon hoi mathētai autou epideixai autō tas oikodomas tou hierou·

paragraphs.text: But he answered and said unto them, See ye not all these things? verily I say unto you, There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ βλέπετε ταῦτα πάντα; ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ ἀφεθῇ ὧδε λίθος ἐπὶ λίθον ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen autois· Ou blepete tauta panta; amēn legō hymin, ou mē aphethē hōde lithos epi lithon hos ou katalythēsetai.

paragraphs.text: And as he sat on the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what [shall be] the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?
paragraphs.original: Καθημένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοῦ Ὄρους τῶν Ἐλαιῶν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ κατʼ ἰδίαν λέγοντες· Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν πότε ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον τῆς σῆς παρουσίας καὶ συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος.
paragraphs.translit: Kathēmenou de autou epi tou Orous tōn Elaiōn prosēlthon autō hoi mathētai katʼ idian legontes· Eipon hēmin pote tauta estai, kai ti to sēmeion tēs sēs parousias kai synteleias tou aiōnos.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man lead you astray.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς πλανήσῃ·
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis ho Iēsous eipen autois· Blepete mē tis hymas planēsē·

paragraphs.text: For many shall come in my name, saying, I am the Christ; and shall lead many astray.
paragraphs.original: πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ χριστός, καὶ πολλοὺς πλανήσουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: polloi gar eleusontai epi tō onomati mou legontes· Egō eimi ho christos, kai pollous planēsousin.

paragraphs.text: And ye shall hear of wars and rumors of wars; see that ye be not troubled: for [these things] must needs come to pass; but the end is not yet.
paragraphs.original: μελλήσετε δὲ ἀκούειν πολέμους καὶ ἀκοὰς πολέμων· ὁρᾶτε, μὴ θροεῖσθε· δεῖ γὰρ γενέσθαι, ἀλλʼ οὔπω ἐστὶν τὸ τέλος.
paragraphs.translit: mellēsete de akouein polemous kai akoas polemōn· horate, mē throeisthe· dei gar genesthai, allʼ oupō estin to telos.

paragraphs.text: For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; and there shall be famines and earthquakes in divers places.
paragraphs.original: ἐγερθήσεται γὰρ ἔθνος ἐπὶ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν, καὶ ἔσονται λιμοὶ καὶ σεισμοὶ κατὰ τόπους·
paragraphs.translit: egerthēsetai gar ethnos epi ethnos kai basileia epi basileian, kai esontai limoi kai seismoi kata topous·

paragraphs.text: But all these things are the beginning of travail.
paragraphs.original: πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων.
paragraphs.translit: panta de tauta archē ōdinōn.

paragraphs.text: Then shall they deliver you up unto tribulation, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all the nations for my name`s sake.
paragraphs.original: Τότε παραδώσουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς θλῖψιν καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.
paragraphs.translit: Tote paradōsousin hymas eis thlipsin kai apoktenousin hymas, kai esesthe misoumenoi hypo pantōn tōn ethnōn dia to onoma mou.

paragraphs.text: And then shall many stumble, and shall deliver up one another, and shall hate one another.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τότε σκανδαλισθήσονται πολλοὶ καὶ ἀλλήλους παραδώσουσιν καὶ μισήσουσιν ἀλλήλους·
paragraphs.translit: kai tote skandalisthēsontai polloi kai allēlous paradōsousin kai misēsousin allēlous·

paragraphs.text: And many false prophets shall arise, and shall lead many astray.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πολλοὶ ψευδοπροφῆται ἐγερθήσονται καὶ πλανήσουσιν πολλούς·
paragraphs.translit: kai polloi pseudoprophētai egerthēsontai kai planēsousin pollous·

paragraphs.text: And because iniquity shall be multiplied, the love of the many shall wax cold.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διὰ τὸ πληθυνθῆναι τὴν ἀνομίαν ψυγήσεται ἡ ἀγάπη τῶν πολλῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai dia to plēthynthēnai tēn anomian psygēsetai hē agapē tōn pollōn.

paragraphs.text: But he that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: ho de hypomeinas eis telos houtos sōthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in the whole world for a testimony unto all the nations; and then shall the end come.
paragraphs.original: καὶ κηρυχθήσεται τοῦτο τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ οἰκουμένῃ εἰς μαρτύριον πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, καὶ τότε ἥξει τὸ τέλος.
paragraphs.translit: kai kērychthēsetai touto to euangelion tēs basileias en holē tē oikoumenē eis martyrion pasin tois ethnesin, kai tote hēxei to telos.

paragraphs.text: When therefore ye see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (let him that readeth understand),
paragraphs.original: Ὅταν οὖν ἴδητε τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Δανιὴλ τοῦ προφήτου ἑστὸς ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ, ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω,
paragraphs.translit: Hotan oun idēte to bdelygma tēs erēmōseōs to rhēthen dia Daniēl tou prophētou hestos en topō hagiō, ho anaginōskōn noeitō,

paragraphs.text: then let them that are in Judaea flee unto the mountains:
paragraphs.original: τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη,
paragraphs.translit: tote hoi en tē Ioudaia pheugetōsan epi ta orē,

paragraphs.text: let him that is on the housetop not go down to take out things that are in his house:
paragraphs.original: ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος μὴ καταβάτω ἆραι τὰ ἐκ τῆς οἰκίας αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: ho epi tou dōmatos mē katabatō arai ta ek tēs oikias autou,

paragraphs.text: and let him that is in the field not return back to take his cloak.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω ὀπίσω ἆραι τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho en tō agrō mē epistrepsatō opisō arai to himation autou.

paragraphs.text: But woe unto them that are with child and to them that give suck in those days!
paragraphs.original: οὐαὶ δὲ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.
paragraphs.translit: ouai de tais en gastri echousais kai tais thēlazousais en ekeinais tais hēmerais.

paragraphs.text: And pray ye that your flight be not in the winter, neither on a sabbath:
paragraphs.original: προσεύχεσθε δὲ ἵνα μὴ γένηται ἡ φυγὴ ὑμῶν χειμῶνος μηδὲ σαββάτῳ·
paragraphs.translit: proseuchesthe de hina mē genētai hē phygē hymōn cheimōnos mēde sabbatō·

paragraphs.text: for then shall be great tribulation, such as hath not been from the beginning of the world until now, no, nor ever shall be.
paragraphs.original: ἔσται γὰρ τότε θλῖψις μεγάλη οἵα οὐ γέγονεν ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς κόσμου ἕως τοῦ νῦν οὐδʼ οὐ μὴ γένηται.
paragraphs.translit: estai gar tote thlipsis megalē hoia ou gegonen apʼ archēs kosmou heōs tou nyn oudʼ ou mē genētai.

paragraphs.text: And except those days had been shortened, no flesh would have been saved: but for the elect`s sake those days shall be shortened.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰ μὴ ἐκολοβώθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι, οὐκ ἂν ἐσώθη πᾶσα σάρξ· διὰ δὲ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς κολοβωθήσονται αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι.
paragraphs.translit: kai ei mē ekolobōthēsan hai hēmerai ekeinai, ouk an esōthē pasa sarx· dia de tous eklektous kolobōthēsontai hai hēmerai ekeinai.

paragraphs.text: Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is the Christ, or, Here; believe [it] not.
paragraphs.original: τότε ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Ἰδοὺ ὧδε ὁ χριστός, ἤ· Ὧδε, μὴ πιστεύσητε·
paragraphs.translit: tote ean tis hymin eipē· Idou hōde ho christos, ē· Hōde, mē pisteusēte·

paragraphs.text: For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall show great signs and wonders; so as to lead astray, if possible, even the elect.
paragraphs.original: ἐγερθήσονται γὰρ ψευδόχριστοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται, καὶ δώσουσιν σημεῖα μεγάλα καὶ τέρατα ὥστε πλανῆσαι εἰ δυνατὸν καὶ τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς·
paragraphs.translit: egerthēsontai gar pseudochristoi kai pseudoprophētai, kai dōsousin sēmeia megala kai terata hōste planēsai ei dynaton kai tous eklektous·

paragraphs.text: Behold, I have told you beforehand.
paragraphs.original: ἰδοὺ προείρηκα ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: idou proeirēka hymin.

paragraphs.text: If therefore they shall say unto you, Behold, he is in the wilderness; go not forth: Behold, he is in the inner chambers; believe [it] not.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν οὖν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν· Ἰδοὺ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἐστίν, μὴ ἐξέλθητε· Ἰδοὺ ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις, μὴ πιστεύσητε·
paragraphs.translit: ean oun eipōsin hymin· Idou en tē erēmō estin, mē exelthēte· Idou en tois tameiois, mē pisteusēte·

paragraphs.text: For as the lightning cometh forth from the east, and is seen even unto the west; so shall be the coming of the Son of man.
paragraphs.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ ἀστραπὴ ἐξέρχεται ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ φαίνεται ἕως δυσμῶν, οὕτως ἔσται ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
paragraphs.translit: hōsper gar hē astrapē exerchetai apo anatolōn kai phainetai heōs dysmōn, houtōs estai hē parousia tou hyiou tou anthrōpou·

paragraphs.text: Wheresoever the carcase is, there will the eagles be gathered together.
paragraphs.original: ὅπου ἐὰν ᾖ τὸ πτῶμα, ἐκεῖ συναχθήσονται οἱ ἀετοί.
paragraphs.translit: hopou ean ē to ptōma, ekei synachthēsontai hoi aetoi.

paragraphs.text: But immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:
paragraphs.original: Εὐθέως δὲ μετὰ τὴν θλῖψιν τῶν ἡμερῶν ἐκείνων ὁ ἥλιος σκοτισθήσεται, καὶ ἡ σελήνη οὐ δώσει τὸ φέγγος αὐτῆς, καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες πεσοῦνται ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: Eutheōs de meta tēn thlipsin tōn hēmerōn ekeinōn ho hēlios skotisthēsetai, kai hē selēnē ou dōsei to phengos autēs, kai hoi asteres pesountai apo tou ouranou, kai hai dynameis tōn ouranōn saleuthēsontai.

paragraphs.text: and then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τότε φανήσεται τὸ σημεῖον τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ τότε κόψονται πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ μετὰ δυνάμεως καὶ δόξης πολλῆς·
paragraphs.translit: kai tote phanēsetai to sēmeion tou hyiou tou anthrōpou en tō ouranō, kai tote kopsontai pasai hai phylai tēs gēs kai opsontai ton hyion tou anthrōpou erchomenon epi tōn nephelōn tou ouranou meta dynameōs kai doxēs pollēs·

paragraphs.text: And he shall send forth his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποστελεῖ τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ μετὰ σάλπιγγος μεγάλης, καὶ ἐπισυνάξουσιν τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ἀνέμων ἀπʼ ἄκρων οὐρανῶν ἕως τῶν ἄκρων αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apostelei tous angelous autou meta salpingos megalēs, kai episynaxousin tous eklektous autou ek tōn tessarōn anemōn apʼ akrōn ouranōn heōs tōn akrōn autōn.

paragraphs.text: Now from the fig tree learn her parable: when her branch is now become tender, and putteth forth its leaves, ye know that the summer is nigh;
paragraphs.original: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς συκῆς μάθετε τὴν παραβολήν· ὅταν ἤδη ὁ κλάδος αὐτῆς γένηται ἁπαλὸς καὶ τὰ φύλλα ἐκφύῃ, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος·
paragraphs.translit: Apo de tēs sykēs mathete tēn parabolēn· hotan ēdē ho klados autēs genētai hapalos kai ta phylla ekphyē, ginōskete hoti engys to theros·

paragraphs.text: even so ye also, when ye see all these things, know ye that he is nigh, [even] at the doors.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε πάντα ταῦτα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἐπὶ θύραις.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kai hymeis, hotan idēte panta tauta, ginōskete hoti engys estin epi thyrais.

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all these things be accomplished.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα ταῦτα γένηται.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin hoti ou mē parelthē hē genea hautē heōs an panta tauta genētai.

paragraphs.text: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.
paragraphs.original: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσεται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρέλθωσιν.
paragraphs.translit: ho ouranos kai hē gē pareleusetai, hoi de logoi mou ou mē parelthōsin.

paragraphs.text: But of that day and hour knoweth no one, not even the angels of heaven, neither the Son, but the Father only.
paragraphs.original: Περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης καὶ ὥρας οὐδεὶς οἶδεν, οὐδὲ οἱ ἄγγελοι τῶν οὐρανῶν οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός, εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ μόνος.
paragraphs.translit: Peri de tēs hēmeras ekeinēs kai hōras oudeis oiden, oude hoi angeloi tōn ouranōn oude ho hyios, ei mē ho patēr monos.

paragraphs.text: And as [were] the days of Noah, so shall be the coming of the Son of man.
paragraphs.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ Νῶε, οὕτως ἔσται ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
paragraphs.translit: hōsper gar hai hēmerai tou Nōe, houtōs estai hē parousia tou hyiou tou anthrōpou·

paragraphs.text: For as in those days which were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark,
paragraphs.original: ὡς γὰρ ἦσαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταῖς πρὸ τοῦ κατακλυσμοῦ τρώγοντες καὶ πίνοντες, γαμοῦντες καὶ γαμίζοντες, ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας εἰσῆλθεν Νῶε εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν,
paragraphs.translit: hōs gar ēsan en tais hēmerais tais pro tou kataklysmou trōgontes kai pinontes, gamountes kai gamizontes, achri hēs hēmeras eisēlthen Nōe eis tēn kibōton,

paragraphs.text: and they knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall be the coming of the Son of man.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν ἕως ἦλθεν ὁ κατακλυσμὸς καὶ ἦρεν ἅπαντας, οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk egnōsan heōs ēlthen ho kataklysmos kai ēren hapantas, houtōs estai kai hē parousia tou hyiou tou anthrōpou.

paragraphs.text: Then shall two man be in the field; one is taken, and one is left:
paragraphs.original: τότε δύο ἔσονται ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, εἷς παραλαμβάνεται καὶ εἷς ἀφίεται·
paragraphs.translit: tote dyo esontai en tō agrō, heis paralambanetai kai heis aphietai·

paragraphs.text: two women [shall be] grinding at the mill; one is taken, and one is left.
paragraphs.original: δύο ἀλήθουσαι ἐν τῷ μύλῳ, μία παραλαμβάνεται καὶ μία ἀφίεται.
paragraphs.translit: dyo alēthousai en tō mylō, mia paralambanetai kai mia aphietai.

paragraphs.text: Watch therefore: for ye know not on what day your Lord cometh.
paragraphs.original: γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε ποίᾳ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ κύριος ὑμῶν ἔρχεται.
paragraphs.translit: grēgoreite oun, hoti ouk oidate poia hēmera ho kyrios hymōn erchetai.

paragraphs.text: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what watch the thief was coming, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken through.
paragraphs.original: ἐκεῖνο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ φυλακῇ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται, ἐγρηγόρησεν ἂν καὶ οὐκ ἂν εἴασεν διορυχθῆναι τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ekeino de ginōskete hoti ei ēdei ho oikodespotēs poia phylakē ho kleptēs erchetai, egrēgorēsen an kai ouk an eiasen diorychthēnai tēn oikian autou.

paragraphs.text: Therefore be ye also ready; for in an hour that ye think not the Son of man cometh.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι, ὅτι ᾗ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὥρᾳ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται.
paragraphs.translit: dia touto kai hymeis ginesthe hetoimoi, hoti hē ou dokeite hōra ho hyios tou anthrōpou erchetai.

paragraphs.text: Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath set over his household, to give them their food in due season?
paragraphs.original: Τίς ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ πιστὸς δοῦλος καὶ φρόνιμος ὃν κατέστησεν ὁ κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκετείας αὐτοῦ τοῦ δοῦναι αὐτοῖς τὴν τροφὴν ἐν καιρῷ;
paragraphs.translit: Tis ara estin ho pistos doulos kai phronimos hon katestēsen ho kyrios epi tēs oiketeias autou tou dounai autois tēn trophēn en kairō;

paragraphs.text: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.
paragraphs.original: μακάριος ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ὃν ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει οὕτως ποιοῦντα·
paragraphs.translit: makarios ho doulos ekeinos hon elthōn ho kyrios autou heurēsei houtōs poiounta·

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto you, that he will set him over all that he hath.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοῦ καταστήσει αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin hoti epi pasin tois hyparchousin autou katastēsei auton.

paragraphs.text: But if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord tarrieth;
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃ ὁ κακὸς δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· Χρονίζει μου ὁ κύριος,
paragraphs.translit: ean de eipē ho kakos doulos ekeinos en tē kardia autou· Chronizei mou ho kyrios,

paragraphs.text: and shall begin to beat his fellow-servants, and shall eat and drink with the drunken;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς συνδούλους αὐτοῦ, ἐσθίῃ δὲ καὶ πίνῃ μετὰ τῶν μεθυόντων,
paragraphs.translit: kai arxētai typtein tous syndoulous autou, esthiē de kai pinē meta tōn methyontōn,

paragraphs.text: the lord of that servant shall come in a day when he expecteth not, and in an hour when he knoweth not,
paragraphs.original: ἥξει ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ οὐ προσδοκᾷ καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ᾗ οὐ γινώσκει,
paragraphs.translit: hēxei ho kyrios tou doulou ekeinou en hēmera hē ou prosdoka kai en hōra hē ou ginōskei,

paragraphs.text: and shall cut him asunder, and appoint his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διχοτομήσει αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ὑποκριτῶν θήσει· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
paragraphs.translit: kai dichotomēsei auton kai to meros autou meta tōn hypokritōn thēsei· ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn.
